audit_findings.title: Cash-tax benefits may be capitalized as permanent owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 cash taxes of $17.546 million versus a $58.184 million tax provision, a computed $40.638 million gap equal to 26.4% of the $153.9 million anchor; exact normalized adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Temporarily low cash taxes raise anchor OE and, if grown without modeling attribute exhaustion, raise every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has federal tax net operating loss carryforwards of approximately $ 191.2 million as of December 31, 2025 and state net operating loss carryforwards spread across various jurisdictions with a combined total of approximately $ 317.0 million as of December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates finite tax attributes, including $191.2 million of federal and $317.0 million of state NOL carryforwards, and a large cash-tax/provision gap. It does not establish that the entire gap is an error because the provision includes deferred timing differences. Nevertheless, perpetuating FY2025 cash taxes could materially overstate value, particularly with terminal value representing 49.7% of base operating PV.
audit_findings.action: Build a tax roll-forward reconciling taxable income, NOL and credit utilization, Section 163(j) effects, deferred-tax reversals and the long-run effective cash-tax rate; rerun all scenarios with temporary tax shields expiring explicitly.

audit_findings.title: Unpaid self-insurance claims may be omitted from both OE and the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $88.1 million reserve and $17.7 million year-over-year increase; treating the $17.7 million increase as an anchor normalization would reduce base value by approximately $5.19 per share before tax interaction
audit_findings.mechanism: CFO-based OE recognizes claim cost when paid rather than when incurred; an abnormal reserve build can inflate anchor OE, while unpaid pre-valuation claims may otherwise escape a mechanically grown forecast.
audit_findings.evidence: Total claims reserves were $ 88.1 million at December 31, 2025 , of which $ 2.4 million is recorded in accrued salaries, wages and benefits, $ 22.8 million is recorded in other accrued liabilities and the remaining long-term portion is recorded in other liabilities in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The reserve increase is demonstrated, but it is not established that the entire $88.1 million should be deducted from the bridge: doing so could double count payments already captured in projected cash flows. The $17.7 million increase is 11.5% of anchor OE, and its computed valuation sensitivity is sufficient to reduce the $45.57 base value to about $40.38, approximately the $40.45 market price. Materiality therefore remains open.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile incurred claims, cash payments, actuarial revisions and reserve movements for several years; rerun OE using normalized cash claims or, alternatively, deduct only the unpaid reserve not captured in forecast cash flows, but do not apply both treatments.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter ignores an active Sesame license termination dispute
audit_findings.mechanism: License termination could change park revenue and margins, require rebranding capital, cause impairment or disruption, and alter royalties and growth assumptions.
audit_findings.evidence: On September 9, 2025, the Company delivered a notice to Sesame asserting that Sesame breached the License Agreement by failing to maximize exposure of the Sesame brand, justifying termination of the License Agreement.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q confirms that mediation did not resolve the dispute: Sesame commenced litigation on March 12, 2026 and seeks termination, while the company moved to dismiss aspects of the claims. The risk is therefore demonstrated, but the record supplies no park-level earnings, rebranding cost or probability-weighted outcome with which to establish materiality. Remaining contractual commitments of up to $11.9 million do not measure the broader operating consequence.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the complaint, dismissal motion and subsequent docket outcome, then quantify revenue, OE, assets and rebranding capital attributable to both standalone parks and the Sesame-themed areas; rerun probability-weighted continuation, amendment and termination cases.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 numerator omits interest on post-year-end borrowing
audit_findings.magnitude: $50.0 million outstanding at June 30, 2026 at 5.38%, implying approximately $2.69 million of annual pre-tax interest and a computed maximum base-value effect of about $0.79 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Incremental revolver interest reduces equity-level OE because interest remains inside the forecast numerator; principal is not separately deducted under the stated method.
audit_findings.evidence: Subsequent to December 31, 2025, SEA borrowed $ 80.0 million on the Revolving Credit Facility for general working capital purposes.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing confirms that borrowing persisted, although only $50.0 million of the original post-year-end draw remained at June 30. The approximately $0.79-per-share pre-tax sensitivity is about 1.7% of the $45.57 base value and is well below the $5.12 gap between base value and the $40.45 market price. On the filed balance alone it is not material to the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Replace the FY2025 interest amount with interest based on the expected average revolver balance, actual 5.38% rate and commitment fees; reconsider materiality only if subsequent evidence shows a materially larger or persistent average borrowing.

audit_findings.title: Unhedged variable-rate debt can materially change the OE anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed sensitivity of $15.2 million annual interest per 100-basis-point SOFR change, equal to 9.9% of anchor OE and approximately $4.46 per share of base value if persistent
audit_findings.mechanism: SOFR changes flow directly through interest expense into equity-level OE and consequently affect forecast cash flows and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: A hypothetical increase in Term SOFR of 100 bps would increase our annual interest expense by approximately $15.2 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The variable-rate debt and lack of hedging are demonstrated; a future rate increase is not. The filed sensitivity is nearly as large as the $5.12 gap between base value and market price, so the unmodeled rate path is reasonably capable of changing the conclusion. Lower rates would increase value and higher rates would decrease it.
audit_findings.action: Rerun bear, base and bull valuations with explicit SOFR paths, actual variable-rate balances and 2029–2031 refinancing spreads, including at least plus and minus 100-basis-point cases without deducting ordinary debt principal separately.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may add operating cash rather than excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum disputed amount of $19.076 million, equal to approximately $0.40 per share or 0.9% of the $45.57 base value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash required for onsite operations, card settlements, seasonal working capital or subsidiary liquidity is not excess cash and should not be added separately to equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash and cash equivalents include cash held at financial institutions as well as operating cash onsite at each theme park to fund daily operations and amounts due from third-party credit card companies with settlement terms of less than four days .
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes that the cash balance includes operating and near-settlement amounts, but does not identify the required portion. Even excluding the entire $19.076 million would reduce base value only from $45.57 to approximately $45.17 and the 30% buy-below level by about $0.28 per share, insufficient by itself to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the cash composition, seasonal minimum-liquidity analysis and subsidiary distribution restrictions; rerun the bridge using only demonstrably distributable excess cash.
